messages.subject: multiple comparisons
parts: As far as I can tell, it seems that you can only have two groups in an experiment (treatment is set to 0 or 1). Is there a way to have more than two groups? What is the recommended approach if you have three groups and you want to compare them all to each other?

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: multiple comparisons
parts:
if you want to do multiple pairwise comparisons the way to do that right now is to organize data into pairs using reorganize() function, then run differentialy methylation commands.

Best,
Altuna
